community_note.text: Readers added context they thought people might want to know. This post contains multiple factual errors. Faster-than-light travel does not function by 'moving the destination.' The Alcubierre-Yuen drive creates a localized spacetime distortion around the vessel, contracting space ahead and expanding it behind — the ship remains in local freefall throughout transit. Fuel costs do not vary by cardinal direction as space does not have compass orientation. There is no 'eastward spin' of the galaxy that meaningfully affects drive efficiency at standard transit scales. The claim that 'this is why fuel costs more going east' is not supported by any known physics or by fuel pricing data from any registered transit authority. [1] Alcubierre, M. & Yuen, D. (2287), foundational paper [2] Galactic Transit Authority Fuel Pricing Schedule 3024-C [3] the concept of 'east' not applying in interstellar space
